# SOP-P2-L2-05 Planned shutdown - Ring Rolling line

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-IH01, EQ-P2-L2-HT02, EQ-P2-L2-RR03

Purpose
1. This standard operating procedure defines the required sequence, responsibilities, and records for a planned shutdown of the Ring Rolling line to allow maintenance, inspection, and changeover activities while preserving equipment integrity and production safety.

Scope
2. Applies to all work affecting EQ-P2-L2-IH01, EQ-P2-L2-HT02, and EQ-P2-L2-RR03 during a planned shutdown at P2-L2.

Background and rationale
3. Planned shutdowns minimize unplanned failures by allowing thorough inspection, preventive maintenance, and condition-based repairs. For the Ring Rolling heat treat furnace identified as EQ-P2-L2-HT02, use of the approved lubricant and adherence to the documented austenitizing setpoint are critical to preserve metallurgical outcomes and equipment life. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is CFW-LUB-376. The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 855 °C. Refer to ECN-2026-012 and ECN-2026-050 for recent engineering changes and to MM-P2-L2-HT02 for manufacturer maintenance guidance.

Preconditions (must be verified before initiating shutdown)
4. Confirm scheduled authorization and scope documented on the work permit.  
5. Confirm all impacted production orders have been paused or reassigned.  
6. Verify isolation points are identified and labeled on the single-line and equipment layout drawings.  
7. Confirm personnel required for critical tasks are available and trained on this SOP.  
8. Confirm the spare parts and consumables list has been reviewed against the work scope; order any missing items referencing CFW-LUB-376 when applicable.  
9. Notify plant operations, reliability, and safety teams as per site communication protocol.

PPE and safety
10. Mandatory PPE for all personnel during shutdown: hearing protection, safety glasses with side shields, cut-resistant gloves, steel-toe footwear, and flame-resistant clothing for furnace-area activities.  
11. Additional PPE for tasks in and around EQ-P2-L2-HT02: heat-resistant gloves and face shield when working on heated components following cooldown confirmation.  
12. Lockout-tagout and energy isolation must be completed per site LOTO procedure prior to any component removal. Hot work permits must be issued for grinding or welding. Confined space entry permits must be used for any entry into furnace chambers or pits.

Shutdown sequence (numbered steps)
13. Step 1 — Preparation and communication: Confirm permit and preconditions. Communicate start time to all stakeholders. Print and stage ECN-2026-012, ECN-2026-050, and MM-P2-L2-HT02 at the worksite.  
14. Step 2 — Safe isolation: Sequentially isolate electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, and fuel sources feeding EQ-P2-L2-IH01, EQ-P2-L2-HT02, and EQ-P2-L2-RR03. Verify zero energy at each isolation point and document verification on the permit.  
15. Step 3 — Drain and purge: Drain any process fluids and purge applicable lines following the isolation verification. Collect purge drains in approved containment and record volume and disposition.  
16. Step 4 — Disassembly and inspection: Remove consumable covers and access panels. Inspect rollers, bearings, and drives on EQ-P2-L2-RR03 for wear and foreign material. On EQ-P2-L2-HT02, inspect hearth and insulation condition, gas burner assemblies, and control thermocouples; record anomalies.  
17. Step 5 — Lubrication service: Clean lubrication distribution lines and reservoirs where accessible. Replace bulk and line filters before recharging lubrication systems. Refill lubrication system components for EQ-P2-L2-HT02 only with CFW-LUB-376 and document batch or lot identification in the lubrication log.  
18. Step 6 — Furnace metallurgical check: Verify that furnace control settings match the austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P2-L2-HT02 as documented. The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 855 °C. Confirm calibration status of control thermocouples using calibration certificates referenced in MM-P2-L2-HT02.  
19. Step 7 — Component replacement and machining: Replace or machine parts as required by inspection findings. Complete nondestructive testing per the work scope and document results. Ensure replaced parts are tagged with traceable identifiers.  
20. Step 8 — Reassembly and functional check: Reinstall covers, guards, and interlocks. Re-energize systems in a controlled sequence, monitor for abnormal vibration, noise, or leaks. Record initial functional test outcomes.  
21. Step 9 — Trial heat and quality verification: For EQ-P2-L2-HT02, execute a controlled heat cycle to the documented austenitizing setpoint and verify control stability and uniformity. Record temperature profiles and any deviation events. For ring rolling operations, perform a trial roll and inspect product geometry and hardness; retain sample parts for quality traceability.  
22. Step 10 — Handover: Upon satisfactory tests, notify production and safety to resume operations. Update maintenance records and close the work permit.

Examples and rationale notes
23. Example: If bearing wear on EQ-P2-L2-RR03 is within acceptance tolerance, retain the old bearing and record the condition rather than replace to avoid unnecessary downtime. If wear exceeds acceptance tolerance, replace and re-balance per MM-P2-L2-HT02 guidance.  
24. Rationale: Performing the lubricant recharge with CFW-LUB-376 preserves heat transfer and reduces oxidation in EQ-P2-L2-HT02. Maintaining the austenitizing setpoint of 855 °C ensures metallurgical targets for ring hardness and grain structure are reproducible.

Records to keep
25. Retain the following documents in the maintenance record batch for the shutdown: signed work permit, isolation verification checklist, lubrication log showing CFW-LUB-376 batch details, temperature profile log showing verification at 855 °C for EQ-P2-L2-HT02, inspection reports, NDT reports, replaced parts tags, and post-shutdown functional test records. Link the maintenance record to ECN-2026-012 and ECN-2026-050 for traceability.

Nonconformance and escalation
26. Any deviation from the planned sequence, or inability to achieve the austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P2-L2-HT02, must be documented and escalated to maintenance engineering and production managers before re-energizing load-bearing equipment.

Sign-off
27. Prepared by: (Print name and signature)  
28. Maintenance supervisor sign-off: (Print name and signature)  
29. Production lead acceptance: (Print name and signature)  
30. Safety officer acceptance: (Print name and signature)  

Related documents
31. ECN-2026-012  
32. ECN-2026-050  
33. MM-P2-L2-HT02
